To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supplementation of polyphenol-rich plant products from grape seed and grape skins or hop as feed ingredients does not influence hepato-protective pathways in healthy piglets.

the supplementation of diets of healthy piglets with polyphenols from either GME or hops did not influence hepatic expression of genes involved in the regulation of inflammation, the antioxidative status, cytoprotection, stress of the ER and the xenobiotics system.

supplementation of diets of healthy piglets with 1% polyphenol-rich GME or SH does not influence hepatically expressed genes and proteins involved in inflammation, the antioxidative and detoxifying system, the unfolded protein response or the xenobiotic metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, whether polyphenol-rich plant products can exert cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and antioxidative effects in the liver.
the question whether polyphenols exert cytoprotective or anti-inflammatory effects on hepatic cells.
the effects of polyphenols on hepatic inflammation and the antioxidative and xenobiotic system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polyphenols in GME or SH do not exert anti-inflammatory effects in piglets, which might be due to the fact that the liver of piglet is not an organ prone to inflammation.
polyphenol-rich plant products do not have any effect in the liver of healthy piglets.

supplementation of diets with plant products containing polyphenols does neither exert negative nor positive influences on the expression of hepatic genes involved in the above-mentioned pathways in healthy piglets, and thus, the effects of polyphenols are limited to the small intestine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the supplementation of GME and SH as sources of dietary polyphenols in piglets did not have any effects on the hepatic expression of genes related to inflammation, antioxidative and cyoprotective system, phase I and II metabolism and endoplasmatic reticulum stress.

supplementation of polyphenol rich plant products from grape seed and grape marcs or hops in the form of 1% feed supplement did not influence gene expression of inflammatory, cytoprotecting, antioxidant and endoplasmatic reticulum stress related pathways in the liver of healthy piglets.

supplementation of GSE or SH did not affect the expression of genes involved in inflammation, antioxidative and cyto-protective pathways and stress of endoplasmic system and xenobiotic metabolism in the liver of healthy piglets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-inflammatory and cyto-protective effects of polyphenol-rich feed supplements observed in the small intestine of piglets are not reflected in the liver.
polyphenols from GME and SH do not have anti-inflammatory or cytoprotective properties in the liver of healthy piglets.
supplementation with GME or hops as sources of polyphenois does not have adverse hepatic effects on healthy piglets.
